hints: Notice what the orange to green colour change tells you, it means dichromate has acted as an oxidising agent so X must be oxidisable.
Look at the two tests on the product together, a positive 2,4-DNPH but negative Tollens result points to one specific carbonyl type.
Work backwards from that carbonyl product to decide whether X must have been a primary alcohol, a secondary alcohol, an aldehyde or a ketone.
walkthrough:
**Interpret the dichromate test**

X turns acidified dichromate from orange to green, so dichromate(VI) is reduced to Cr(III). That means X itself is oxidised.

$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} (\text{orange}) \rightarrow \text{Cr}^{3+} (\text{green})$$

**Identify the organic product**

The product gives no change with Tollens reagent, so it is not an aldehyde. It gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, so it does contain a C=O group.

Not aldehyde + contains C=O = ketone. So the oxidation product is a ketone.

**Work back to X**

Remember the oxidation pattern: primary alcohol gives aldehyde then carboxylic acid, secondary alcohol gives ketone, tertiary alcohol and ketone and carboxylic acid are not oxidised by this reagent.

$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Choose the secondary alcohol**

Only a secondary alcohol can be oxidised to a ketone. Cyclohexanol is a secondary alcohol and oxidises to cyclohexanone, which fits both test results perfectly.

options.A: Cyclohexanone is a ketone. Ketones resist further oxidation by heated $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{H}^+$, so there would be no orange to green change. This contradicts the first observation.
options.B: This aldehyde would be oxidised (orange to green) but to a carboxylic acid, not to a ketone. A carboxylic acid gives no precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, so it fails the second test.
options.C: This is a carboxylic acid. It is already fully oxidised for this reagent, so no orange to green change would occur. Students sometimes confuse the $\text{COOH}$ group with an alcohol, but it cannot be oxidised further.
options.D: Cyclohexanol is a secondary alcohol. It is oxidised by heated $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{H}^+$ to cyclohexanone, giving the orange to green change. Cyclohexanone is a ketone, so it gives no reaction with Tollens reagent but a positive orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine.
